facts: Global flags precede the subcommand. `colab --auth=adc sessions` works; `colab sessions --auth=adc` -> `No such option: --auth`.
`--auth` selects a credential MECHANISM, not an account. Identity comes from `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG`.
No `colab whoami`. ADC files often carry an empty `account` field; identity is not readable after the fact.
`exec` never takes code positionally, in any version. stdin or `-f`.
`--timeout` bounds code execution only, not a lost websocket. Wrap every call in coreutils `timeout`.
Builds share `sessions.json`; a session created by one build is usable by another.
The binary installs to `~/.local/bin`, which is absent from a non-login shell PATH.

global_flags.meaning: credential strategy. oauth2 (default) = CLI's own installed-app flow + token.json; adc = Application Default Credentials.
CLI chatter to stderr; stdout stays pipeable.

session lifecycle.note: list server-side assignments AND reconcile the local store: prunes local rows the calling account cannot see, refreshes proxy tokens. Bare only -- `colab sessions list` is an error.
one session's state. `-s` takes the local label, never an endpoint id.
browser URL attaching the Colab frontend to your existing VM. Pipeable.
0.7.x only. CU balance, burn rate, active assignment count. No side effects on the local store.

execution.note: run code in the session kernel. Code via stdin or -f only.
0.7.x only. SSH into the runtime, incl. an OpenSSH ProxyCommand bridge.
allocate a fresh VM, run a local script, release. Works as a shebang interpreter.

files.note: one file. Large uploads fail intermittently -- chunk them.
pip install on the VM. `-r requirements.txt` works.

meta.cmd: colab log [-s NAME] [-n N] [-t TYPE] [-o OUT]
meta.note: session history. `--output` infers format from suffix: .ipynb, .md, .txt, .jsonl. Agent audit trail.
check PyPI; --install upgrades in place (Linux only).

new_flags.values: high-RAM shape. Honoured for CPU/T4/A100; ignored for L4 and both TPUs (single shape each). 0.7.x only.

exec_flags.note: code-execution timeout, default 30 s. Does not bound a lost websocket.
0.7.x only. Env var in the remote kernel. Repeatable.

run_flags: --gpu/--tpu/--high-mem, -s, --keep, --timeout, --env; script_args after the path arrive as sys.argv[1:]

version_diff.note: 0.6.0 handles die ~1 h; 0.7.x refreshes with a 5-min margin

internals.import: from colab_cli.common import state, AuthProvider, SessionState

objects.name: state.client
objects.note: authorized client. Methods: assign, unassign(endpoint), list_assignments(), get_consumption_user_info(). Constructing it yourself from raw ADC credentials fails with `'Credentials' object has no attribute 'request'`.

objects.name: ListedAssignment
objects.note: endpoint, accelerator, variant, machine_shape, runtime_proxy_info (token, url, tokenExpiresInSeconds). list_assignments() mints a fresh proxy token per call.

objects.name: SessionState
objects.note: one row of sessions.json. Required: name, token, url, endpoint. Optional: token_expires_at, variant, accelerator, machine_shape, kernel_id, session_id, last_execution, running.

internals.trap: accelerator/variant/machine_shape are ENUMS on an assignment and `str` on SessionState. pydantic v2 will not coerce them; a refused row makes the whole store fail closed. Write enum NAMES (`.name`), not values.

examples.title: account selection
examples.code:
CLOUDSDK_CONFIG=~/.config/gcloud-A colab --auth=adc sessions   # account A
CLOUDSDK_CONFIG=~/.config/gcloud-B colab --auth=adc sessions   # account B

examples.title: exec: stdin or -f, never positional
examples.code:
colab exec -s s1 'print(1+1)'          # Error: Got unexpected extra argument(s)
echo 'print(6*7)' | colab exec -s s1    # ok
colab exec -s s1 -f ./job.py           # ok

examples.title: colab run as a shebang interpreter
two builds side by side
examples.code:
uv venv --python 3.12 ~/colab-075
uv pip install --python ~/colab-075/bin/python 'google-colab-cli==0.7.5'
~/colab-075/bin/colab version   # leaves a shared `uv tool` install untouched

examples.title: enumerate assignments
examples.code:
from colab_cli.common import state, AuthProvider
state.auth_provider = AuthProvider.OAUTH2
for a in state.client.list_assignments():
    print(a.endpoint, a.accelerator, a.machine_shape, a.runtime_proxy_info.token[:12])
